chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halby, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about dyeing the hair, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) had dyed, and Al-Husayn ibn Ali, and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) with Al-Katam.'

key_terms.الْكَتَم: Al-Katam, a plant used for dyeing

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet and Imams use to dye their hair according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi not only confirms the permissibility of hair dyeing but specifically highlights the use of 'Al-Katam' (a type of dye, often identified as henna or a similar plant) by the Prophet, Al-Husayn, and Imam al-Baqir, establishing a strong prophetic precedent (sunnah) in Shia tradition. It underscores the importance of maintaining a youthful and dignified appearance as an act of following the Ahl al-Bayt, distinguishing their practice from the color black which was discouraged for men. The narration serves as a foundational text for fiqh rulings on personal grooming, emphasizing that aesthetic enhancement is a meritorious act when aligned with the practices of the Imams.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about dyeing the hair, so heasws said: ‘The Prophetsaww had dyed, and Aliasws Husayn Bin Aliasws, and Abu Ja’farasws with Al-Katam (a dyeing plant)’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about applying dye to the hairs. He (the Imam) said, ‘The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, applied it as well as al-Husayn and abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, with al- Katam (a plant that looks like myrtle and gives out a black dye).”’
